source_text: Εἰ δὲ διὰ τῶν κατὰ φύσιν πρώτων καὶ τῶν τούτοις ἑπομένων δέδεικται τῶν ἐξητασμένων ἕκαστον, εὔδηλον ὅτι καὶ δυνατὸν καὶ βουλητὸν καὶ ἄξιον τοῦ δημιουργήσαντος ἔργον ἡ τῶν διαλυθέντων σωμάτων ἀνάστασις· διὰ γὰρ τούτων ἐδείχθη ψεῦδος τὸ τούτοις ἀντικείμενον καὶ τὸ τῶν ἀπιστούντων παράλογον. Τί γὰρ δεῖ λέγειν περὶ τῆς ἑκάστου αὐτῶν πρὸς ἕκαστον ἀντιστροφῆς καὶ τῆς πρὸς ἄλληλα συναφείας, εἴ γε δεῖ καὶ συνάφειαν εἰπεῖν, ὡς ἑτερότητί τινι κεχωρισμένων, οὐχὶ δὲ καὶ τὸ δυνατὸν λέγειν βουλητόν, καὶ τὸ τῷ θεῷ βουλητὸν πάντως εἶναι δυνατόν, καὶ κατὰ τὴν τοῦ βουληθέντος ἀξίαν; Καὶ ὅτι μὲν ἕτερος ὁ περὶ τῆς ἀληθείας λόγος, ἕτερος δὲ ὁ ὑπὲρ τῆς ἀληθείας, εἴρηται διὰ τῶν προλαβόντων μετρίως, οἶς τε διενήνοχεν ἑκάτερος, καὶ πότε καὶ πρὸς τίνας ἔχει τὸ χρήσιμον· κωλύει δὲ ἴσως οὐδέν, τῆς τε κοινῆς ἀσφαλείας ἕνεκεν καὶ τῆς τῶν εἰρημένων πρὸς τὰ λειπόμενα συναφείας, ἀπ᾿ αὐτῶν τούτων καὶ τῶν τούτοις προσηκόντων πάλιν ποιήσασθαι τὴν ἀρχήν. Προσῆκε δὲ τῷ μὲν τὸ πρωτεύειν κατὰ φύσιν, τῷ δὲ τὸ δορυφορεῖν τὸν πρῶτον ὁδοποιεῖν τε καὶ προανείργειν πᾶν ὁπόσον ἐμποδὼν καὶ πρόσαντες. Ὁ μὲν γὰρ περὶ τῆς ἀληθείας λόγος, ἀναγκαῖος ὢν πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις πρὸς ἀσφάλειαν καὶ σωτηρίαν, πρωτοστατεῖ καὶ τῇ φύσει καὶ τῇ τάξει καὶ τῇ χρείᾳ· τῇ φύσει μέν, ὡς τὴν τῶν πραγμάτων γνῶσιν παρεχόμενος, τῇ τάξει δέ, ὡς ἐν τούτοις καὶ ἅμα τούτοις ὑπάρχων ὦν γίνεται μηνυτής, τῇ χρείᾳ δέ, ὡς τῆς ἀσφαλείας καὶ τῆς σωτηρίας τοῖς γινώσκουσι γινόμενος πρόξενος. Ὁ δ᾿ ὑπὲρ τῆς ἀληθείας φύσει τε καὶ δυνάμει καταδεέστερος, ἔλαττον γὰρ τὸ τὸ ψεῦδος ἐλέγχειν τοῦ τὴν ἀλήθειαν κρατύνειν· καὶ τάξει δεύτερος, κατὰ γὰρ τῶν ψευδοδοξούντων ἔχει τὴν ἰσχύν· ψευδοδοξία δὲ ἐξ ἐπισπορᾶς ἐπεφύη καὶ παραφθορᾶς. Ἀλλὰ δὴ καὶ τούτων οὕτως ἐχόντων προτάττεται πολλάκις καὶ γίνεταί ποτε χρειωδέστερος, ὡς ἀναιρῶν καὶ προκαθαίρων τὴν ἐνοχλοῦσάν τισιν ἀπιστίαν καὶ τοῖς ἄρτι προσιοῦσι τὴν ἀμφιβολίαν ἢ ψευδοδοξίαν. Καὶ πρὸς ἓν μὲν ἑκάτερος ἀναφέρεται τέλος· εἰς γὰρ τὴν εὐσέβειαν ἔχει τὴν ἀναφορὰν ὅ τε τὸ ψεῦδος ἐλέγχων καὶ ὁ τὴν ἀλήθειαν κρατύνων· οὐ μὴν καὶ καθάπαξ ἕν εἰσιν, ἀλλ᾿ ὁ μὲν ἀναγκαῖος, ὡς ἔφην, πᾶσι τοῖς πιστεύουσι καὶ τοῖς τῆς ἀληθείας καὶ τῆς ἰδίας σωτηρίας φροντίζουσιν, ὁ δ᾿ ἔστιν ὅτε καὶ τισι καὶ πρός τινας γίνεται χρειωδέστερος. Καὶ ταῦτα μὲν ἡμῖν κεφαλαιωδῶς προειρήσθω πρὸς ὑπόμνησιν τῶν ἤδη λεχθέντων. Ἰτέον δὲ ἐπὶ τὸ προκείμενον, καὶ δεικτέον ἀληθῆ τὸν περὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως λόγον ἀπό τε τῆς αἰτίας αὐτῆς, καθ᾿ ἣν καὶ δι᾿ ἣν ὁ πρῶτος γέγονεν ἄνθρωπος οἵ τε μετ᾿ ἐκεῖνον, εἰ καὶ μὴ κατὰ τὸν ὅμοιον γεγόνασι τρόπον, ἀπό τε τῆς κοινῆς πάντων ἀνθρώπων ὡς ἀνθρώπων φύσεως, ἔτι δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς τοῦ ποιήσαντος ἐπὶ τούτοις κρίσεως, καθ᾿ ὅσον ἕκαστος ἔζησε χρόνον καὶ καθ᾿ οὓς ἐπολιτεύσατο νόμους, ἣν οὐκ ἄν τις ἀμφισβητήσειεν εἶναι δικαίαν.
pass_a_gloss: If through the first things according to nature and the things following these it has been shown that each of the things examined is evident, it is clear that also the resurrection of the dissolved bodies is possible and willed and worthy of the one who created the work; for through these things the falsehood opposed to these things and the unreasonable thing of the unbelievers has been shown. For what need is there to speak about the turning of each of these things to each one and their connection to each other, if indeed it is necessary to speak also of connection, as if they have been separated by some difference, and not also that the possible thing is willed, and the thing willed by God is certainly possible, and according to the worthiness of the thing willed? And that the discourse about truth is one thing, and the discourse on behalf of truth is another thing, has been said moderately by those who have spoken before me, to whom each has been useful, and when and to whom it has been useful; but perhaps it hinders nothing, for the sake of common safety and the connection of the things said to the things remaining, to make the beginning again from these things and the things suitable to them. It was fitting for the one to lead according to nature, and for the other to follow the first and to make a way and to remove every hindrance and obstacle. For the discourse about truth, being necessary for all people for safety and salvation, takes the first place in nature and order and need; in nature, as providing the knowledge of things, in order, as being in these things and at the same time with them, becoming a messenger, in need, as becoming a provider of safety and salvation to those who know. The discourse on behalf of truth is weaker in nature and power, for it is less to refute falsehood than to confirm truth; and it is second in order, for it has power against those who hold false opinions; false opinion has arisen from ignorance and corruption. But even though these things are so, it is often preferred and becomes more necessary, as removing and purifying the unbelief that troubles some and the doubt or false opinion of those who are just coming. And each has a reference to one end; for both the one refuting falsehood and the one confirming truth have a reference to piety; not that they are the same, but the one is necessary, as I said, for all who believe and care about truth and their own salvation, and the other becomes more necessary for some and in certain circumstances. Let these things be said by us in summary as a reminder of the things already said. We must proceed to the subject before us, and show that the discourse about resurrection is true, from the cause of it, according to which and through which the first human being was made and those after him, even if not in the same way, and from the common nature of all human beings as human beings, and also from the judgment of the one who made them, according to how long each lived and the laws they lived under, which no one would dispute is just.
pass_b_english: If the first principles of nature and what follows from them have demonstrated each point under examination, it is evident that the resurrection of dissolved bodies is possible, willed, and worthy of the Creator; for by these very principles the falsehood opposed to them and the unreasonableness of the unbelievers have been exposed. Why should we elaborate on how each of these principles relates to the others and their interconnection, as if they were separated by some difference? We need not also argue that what is possible is willed, that what God wills is certainly possible, and that this accords with the worthiness of what is willed. The distinction between discourse about truth and discourse on behalf of truth has been stated with moderation by earlier writers, who clarified the respective uses of each, and when and to whom each is useful. Yet nothing prevents us from beginning again from these principles and their corollaries, for the sake of common safety and the continuity of what has been said with what remains. It belongs to the one discourse to lead by nature, and to the other to attend the first, clearing the way and removing every hindrance and obstacle. For the discourse about truth, being necessary for all people for safety and salvation, takes first place by nature, order, and need: by nature, as it provides knowledge of reality; by order, as it exists within and alongside these realities, serving as their herald; by need, as it secures safety and salvation for those who know. The discourse on behalf of truth is weaker by nature and power, since refuting falsehood is a lesser task than confirming truth; it is second in order, for its force operates against those who hold false opinions, and false opinion springs from ignorance and corruption. Yet even so, this second discourse is often preferred and becomes more necessary, as it removes and purifies the unbelief that troubles some and the doubt or false opinion of those just approaching. Both discourses refer to one end: both the one refuting falsehood and the one confirming truth aim at piety. They are not identical, however; the one is necessary, as I said, for all who believe and care for truth and their own salvation, while the other becomes more necessary for certain people and in certain circumstances. Let these things stand as a summary reminder of what has been said. We must now proceed to the subject at hand and demonstrate that the discourse about the resurrection is true, drawing from its cause — the cause according to which and through which the first human being came to be, and those after him, even if not in the same manner — from the common nature shared by all human beings as human beings, and from the judgment of the Maker upon them, according to the length of each one's life and the laws under which each conducted himself, a judgment no one would dispute is just.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex distinctions made by Athenagoras between the 'discourse about truth' (ὁ περὶ τῆς ἀληθείας λόγος) and the 'discourse on behalf of truth' (ὁ ὑπὲρ τῆς ἀληθείας λόγος). Pass A preserves the clause structure and nuances of the Greek, while Pass B provides a fluent rendering that maintains the theological and logical distinctions (e.g., 'refuting falsehood' vs 'confirming truth'). All arguments regarding the necessity, nature, order, and need of these discourses are present. The concluding section regarding the cause of resurrection and the judgment of the Maker is fully rendered.

The translation accurately reflects the Greek text, preserving the meaning, structure, and key theological concepts. The inline citations are correctly matched to the content, and the title appropriately captures the thought of the passage. No omissions, additions, or distortions are present in the translation.
